newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BRL Hardy sees strong early 97 sales.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BRL Hardy sees strong early 97 sales.

text.p: Winemaker BRL Hardy Ltd said on Thursday strong sales had continued in Australia and overseas since the end of 1996, giving the company confidence of further success through the rest of 1997.

"However, limited product availability, especially red wine, is expected to remain a challenge for us and the industry for the next few years," BRL managing director Stephen Millar said in the group's full year result.
BRL Hardy said the continuation of strong sales in the first two months of this year augurs well for further success in 1997, both in Australia and overseas.

"The record 1996 vintage has enabled us to complete the year with satisfactory levels of stocks on hand, although the effect of poor 1995 vintage on red wine production will limit the growth of red wine sales in both 1997 and 1998," BRL Hardy said.

It said the 1997 Australian vintage is expected by the industry to be around 800,000 tonnes, about 10 percent down on 1996 as a result of some early frosts and seasonal fluctuations but still significantly above the 1995 vintage.
"We anticipate that our vintage intake will also be down a similar percentage against 1996, but preferred varieties are expected to increase by at least 10 percent," BRL Hardy said.
BRL Hardy earlier reported a 33 percent rise in net profit to A$23.07 million in calendar 1996.
Sales rose eight percent to A$309.02 million in the year, with 29 percent of total sales accounted for by international sales.
At 1.35 p.m. (0235 GMT), BRL Hardy shares were one cent up at A$3.16.
